0.long_answer: Hidradenitis suppurativa, a chronic inflammatory skin disease marked by painful lumps in regions such as the underarms, groin, and buttocks, is typically staged using the Hurley staging system. This system categorizes the severity of the disease into three stages based on factors like the extent of abscesses, sinus tracts, scarring, and overall lesion distribution, which assists clinicians in determining the most appropriate treatment approach. In cases of severe or refractory disease, treatments including the chimeric monoclonal antibody infliximab may be employed.
